source: AHN5, Dutch national airborne laser scan (Kadaster, open data via PDOK), sub-tiles 25GN1_01 and 25EZ1_21
encoding: interleaved int8 x, int8 y, uint8 z, uint8 category (0=ground, 1=canopy, 2=building roof); 4 bytes/point
assumptions: ground = median z of classification 2 per 1.5 m cell
canopy = highest classification-1 return per 1 m cell, at least 2 m above the local ground median; AHN does not label vegetation, so this is height above ground, not a species or leaf attribute
building = highest classification-6 return per 1.2 m cell
water gives the laser no return, so the canal is the gap in the ground; bridges (26) excluded
0 returns above 45 m NAP dropped (a single spire), so the houses keep their proportions
uniform random thinning to the point budget; no derived quantity computed
